paragraphs.source_en: This time, he began twisting his moustache again. To begin with, his moustache was never an orderly growth; each hair grew in an attitude of self-government. Even in an age when individualism is fashionable, for them to be so uneven and each go its own way must cause their owner a degree of trouble worthy of sympathy. Taking due note of this, the master has lately been giving his moustache strict training, striving to arrange it as systematically as possible. The fruits of the master's earnest efforts have not been in vain. Recently the pace of his moustache has at last become somewhat coordinated, enough for him to boast, 'In the past I merely had a moustache growing; now I am cultivating one.' When earnestness begins to show results it is naturally encouraged; seeing that his moustache had a promising future, the master, morning or evening, whenever his hands were idle, would unfailingly set about disciplining it. His ambition was to grow a moustache like His Majesty the German Emperor's, one possessed of an ardent aspiration upward. Thus, whether the pores pointed sideways or downward, he paid not the least heed, but gathered them all together in one handful and pulled them as hard as he could upward. His moustache must surely feel quite at a loss under such treatment. Even its owner, my master, sometimes finds it quite painful. Still, the essential point is training. Whether the moustache likes it or not, he yanks it forcibly upward. To an outsider it looks like an incomprehensible hobby, yet the person concerned regards it as perfectly natural. It is much the same as educators who forcibly bend the natural character of their pupils and boast, 'Behold my skill,' and so there is no reason to criticize it at all.

paragraphs.source_en: Just as the master was training his moustache with wholehearted zeal, Osan, the maid with the many-angled head, came from the kitchen into the study, thrust out her red hand, and said, 'A letter has come for you.' The master, his right hand still clutching his moustache and his left holding the mirror, turned toward the study entrance without changing his pose. The instant Osan saw the moustache, its two strokes of the character 'eight' ordered to stand up at the tips, she drew back at once into the kitchen, leaned against the lid of the rice kettle, and burst into endless laughter. The master was quite unconcerned; leisurely he lowered the mirror and picked up the mail that had been brought in. The first letter was printed in type, and the wording appeared somehow imposing. When the master read it, he found that the sender was an aristocrat, and it said:

paragraphs.source_en: Dear Sir, we respectfully offer our congratulations on your continued good fortune and well-being. Looking back, the Russo-Japanese War, riding the momentum of victory after victory, has at last brought about the restoration of peace. Already more than half of our loyal, brave, and righteous officers and men have returned in triumph, raising songs of victory amid cries of 'Banzai!' How can the people's joy be expressed in words? When, some time ago, the great imperial edict declaring war was promulgated, our valiant soldiers, dedicating themselves to public service, remained long in a foreign land ten thousand miles away, endured the hardships of heat and cold, and devoted themselves wholly to battle; their utmost sincerity in offering their lives to the nation must be engraved forever upon our hearts, not to be forgotten for even a moment. The triumphant return of the army will, moreover, be completed by the end of this month. Accordingly, this association proposes to hold, on the twenty-fifth of next month, a grand celebration of triumph for the more than one thousand officers, noncommissioned officers, and soldiers of this district who went to the front, representing all the residents of our district, while also consoling the bereaved families of servicemen. We desire to welcome this occasion with sincere enthusiasm and thereby express our modest gratitude; and should we receive your support and be fortunate enough to carry out this splendid ceremony, no greater honor could come to this association. We therefore earnestly request your vigorous approval and generous contributions. Respectfully yours.

paragraphs.source_en: After reading it through silently, the master immediately rolled the letter back into its envelope and paid it no further attention. He will probably make no donation. The other day, for the relief fund for the agricultural disaster in the northeast, he contributed either two yen or three. Since then he has gone about telling everyone that a donation had been taken from him; yet, since it was a donation, he must surely have handed it over of his own accord, not had it taken from him. It was not as though a thief had broken in and carried something off, so to say it was taken is plainly inappropriate. Nevertheless, the master seems to think of it as though he had been robbed. Therefore, no matter that this is some welcome celebration for soldiers, and no matter that an aristocratic gentleman is its sponsor, unless they came at him with threats, he is hardly the sort of man to hand over money on the strength of a single printed notice. From the master's point of view, before welcoming the soldiers, he would rather have himself welcomed first. Once he had been welcomed, he could welcome almost anyone. It appears that, while he still worries morning and evening about his own livelihood, he has resolved to leave the business of welcoming to aristocratic gentlemen.
